owner.description: The first owner's account, which is an instance admin

setup_code.description: The setup code, which the server writes to its log while setup is pending, as 7K2M-Q9XD-4RTB-H8VW. Case, hyphens, and spaces do not matter, and O is read as 0, and I and L as 1.

signup_policy.description: Who can register an account once setup has completed: closed (no one), invite (people holding an invitation), or open (anyone). Without it, closed. STORYCREEP_SIGNUP overrides it for as long as it is set, as GET /api/v1/setup says.

smtp.description: The SMTP server that the instance sends its email through: the links that verify an email address and reset a password. Without it, the instance sends no email, and an instance admin gives out the links as text. STORYCREEP_SMTP_URL overrides it for as long as it is set, as GET /api/v1/setup says. Setup does not connect to it.

workspace.description: The first workspace, which the owner owns, and which is the owner's personal workspace. Its default locale is STORYCREEP_DEFAULT_LOCALE.

owner_id.description: The ID of the owner's account, which signs in with POST /api/v1/auth/login

default_locale.description: The workspace's default locale, as a BCP 47 tag of a locale that the server has a catalog for. Without it, the locale of the request: the one that its Accept-Language prefers among those, or else STORYCREEP_DEFAULT_LOCALE.

name.description: The workspace's name, of 1 to 100 characters, not all of them blank, and without control characters, bidirectional controls and line separators among them. White space around it is removed.

slug.description: The workspace's slug: groups of lowercase ASCII letters and digits joined by single hyphens, of at most 64 characters, and not a reserved word, or the answer is 422 slug_invalid; if another workspace has it, the answer is 409 slug_taken. Without it, the slug is derived from the name: its letters and digits in lowercase ASCII, without accents, each run of other characters a hyphen, cut to 64 characters, or workspace if the name has none. If another workspace has that slug, or it is a reserved word, -2, -3, and so on up to -10 is added, and after that a random suffix of 8 lowercase letters and digits.

code.description: A stable error code; docs/error-codes.md lists them

details.description: More about the error, for programs; the code decides the keys

message.description: What went wrong, for people, in the language that the Content-Language header names

request_id.description: The request's ID, which the server's log records it under

email_configured.description: Whether the instance sends email, through the SMTP server of STORYCREEP_SMTP_URL or of first-run setup. Without it, a page says that email is not configured: the links that reset a password and verify an email address are not emailed, and an instance admin gives them out as text.

email.description: The email address of the account, in any case

url.description: The link, which opens the web app's page that uses it, with its token in the URL's fragment. Whoever holds it can use it, so give it only to the account's user.

email.description: The account's email address, in any case

default_locale.description: The workspace's default locale, as a BCP 47 tag of a locale that the server has a catalog for

membership_id.description: The ID of the signed-in user's membership of the workspace

role.description: The role of the signed-in user's membership. A guest acts only on the projects granted to them, and GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id} answers them with 404 not_found.

slug.description: The workspace's slug, which is unique on the instance

updated_at.description: When its name, slug, or settings last changed

new_password.description: The new password: at least 12 characters, and not one of the most common passwords, or the answer is weak_password

email.description: The email address of the account whose password to reset, in any case

display_name.description: The name that other people see, of 1 to 100 characters, not all of them blank, and without control characters, bidirectional controls and line separators among them. White space around it is removed.

email.description: The account's email address, which signs in: an address alone, as jo@example.com, of at most 254 bytes, without spaces or characters that are not printed. Addresses compare without regard to case or to how their characters are composed.

password.description: The password: at least 12 characters, and not one of the most common passwords, or the answer is weak_password.

new_password.description: The new password: at least 12 characters, and not one of the most common passwords, or the answer is weak_password

token.description: The token of the link that resets the password: what follows token= in the fragment of the URL that the link opens

current.description: Whether it is the session of the request

expires_at.description: When it ends at the latest, however often it is used: STORYCREEP_SESSION_LIFETIME after its user signed in, or the lifetime in force when its user signed in, if that was shorter

idle_expires_at.description: When it ends unless it is used before: STORYCREEP_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT after its last use, or at expires_at if that is sooner

ip.description: The IP address that its user signed in from: the address that the connection came from, or, if that is one of STORYCREEP_TRUSTED_PROXIES, the client's address that the proxies forwarded

last_seen_at.description: When it was last used, to the minute

user_agent.description: The User-Agent header of the client that its user signed in with

signup_policy.description: The signup policy that the configuration sets, if it sets one, or else the one that setup records when the request names none: closed.

signup_policy_fixed.description: Whether the configuration sets the signup policy, with STORYCREEP_SIGNUP, or because the instance is hosted, which then overrides the policy that setup records, for as long as it sets it. A setup screen offers no choice of policy then.

smtp_fixed.description: Whether the configuration sets the SMTP server, with STORYCREEP_SMTP_URL, which then overrides the one that setup records, for as long as it sets it. A setup screen asks for no SMTP server then.

display_name.description: The owner's display name, as for POST /api/v1/auth/register

email.description: The owner's email address, which signs in, as for POST /api/v1/auth/register

password.description: The owner's password: at least 12 characters, and not one of the most common passwords, or the answer is weak_password.

from.description: The address that the instance's email comes from, alone or with a name, as Storycreep <noreply@example.com>, which the server must let it send from

host.description: The SMTP server's host name or IP address

password.description: The password that signs in to the server, with the username

port.description: The SMTP server's port, as 587 for starttls or 465 for tls

security.description: How the connection is protected: tls, from its start; starttls, which the server must offer, before anything is sent; or none, for a relay on the same host or network, which then cannot sign in unless it is on localhost, 127.0.0.1, or ::1

username.description: The username that signs in to the server, with PLAIN or LOGIN, with the password; without it, the server is not signed in to

name.description: The workspace's name, as for POST /api/v1/workspaces

slug.description: The workspace's slug, as for POST /api/v1/workspaces, with the same errors. Without it, the slug is derived from the name.

csrf_token.description: The session's CSRF token: every request made with the session that changes something, with a method other than GET, HEAD, or OPTIONS, sends it in its X-CSRF-Token header, or is answered with 403 csrf_failed. slug.description: The workspace's new slug, as for POST /api/v1/workspaces, with the same errors. A slug that the workspace has already is kept, as a reserved word that a later release added to the list is.

token.description: The token of the link that verifies the email address: what follows token= in the fragment of the URL that the link opens

post.description: Returns a link that resets the password of the active account that the email address belongs to, which lasts an hour, and is used once with POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset/confirm. It is for an instance that sends no email, whose links an instance admin gives out instead, to the account's user alone, because whoever holds a link can use it; an instance that sends email answers 403 email_configured. A user who is not an instance admin, such as a workspace's owner or admin, is answered with 403 instance_admin_required, whatever the request holds. An address that belongs to no active account is answered with 404 not_found. The audit log records the issue. It needs a signed-in user: the session cookie that POST /api/v1/auth/login sets, or the answer is 401 unauthenticated. It changes something, so it also needs the session's CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header, or the answer is 403 csrf_failed. Signing in, registering, changing a password, completing first-run setup, asking for a link that resets a password or verifies an email address, using one, and an instance admin's taking one as text share a rate limit of 20 requests a minute for each IP address. Registering and asking for a link that resets a password also have one of 10 a minute for each email address, and changing a password, asking for a link that verifies the signed-in account's email address, and an instance admin's taking a link as text one of 10 a minute for each account. The RateLimit headers say how much of the limit of the IP address, or of the account, is left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.reason is rate, whose RateLimit headers report the limit that it is over, that of the email address included, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

post.summary: Ask for a link that verifies the account's email address

post.description: Signs in with an account's email address and password, and starts a session, whose secret the Set-Cookie header gives the client, and whose CSRF token the body holds. The account's first sign-in also gives it its personal workspace, named after its display name, which it owns; GET /api/v1/workspaces lists it. Where the instance always sends email, as hosted mode does, that is the first sign-in once the account's email address is verified, or the verification itself. An address of no account, a wrong password, and an account that cannot sign in, such as a suspended one, are all answered with 401 invalid_credentials, after the same work, so that the answer does not tell them apart. A request that a browser's Sec-Fetch-Site header says comes from another site, or from another origin of the same site, is answered with 403 csrf_failed; browsers send that header only to https URLs and to loopback addresses, such as localhost. After 10 failed sign-ins in a row with an email address, whether or not it belongs to an account, the address is locked for a minute, and each further failure, once a lock ends, locks it for twice as long as the lock before, up to 15 minutes: while it is locked, every sign-in with it is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.reason is locked, even with the right password. A successful sign-in forgets the failures, and so do 24 hours without one. Signing in, registering, changing a password, completing first-run setup, asking for a link that resets a password or verifies an email address, using one, and an instance admin's taking one as text share a rate limit of 20 requests a minute for each IP address. Registering and asking for a link that resets a password also have one of 10 a minute for each email address, and changing a password, asking for a link that verifies the signed-in account's email address, and an instance admin's taking a link as text one of 10 a minute for each account. The RateLimit headers say how much of the limit of the IP address, or of the account, is left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.reason is rate, whose RateLimit headers report the limit that it is over, that of the email address included, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

post.description: Changes the signed-in account's password, if current_password is the account's, or the answer is 403 wrong_password. The new password must have at least 12 characters, counted as Unicode code points once it is in NFKC, and must not be one of the 10,000 most common passwords, or the answer is 422 weak_password. Changing it revokes every other session of the account, stops the account's links that reset its password from working, and gives the session of the request a new secret, in the Set-Cookie header, and a new CSRF token, in the body, so that the old ones are no longer valid. It needs a signed-in user: the session cookie that POST /api/v1/auth/login sets, or the answer is 401 unauthenticated. It changes something, so it also needs the session's CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header, or the answer is 403 csrf_failed. post.summary: Ask for a link that resets a password

post.description: Replaces the password of the account of a link that resets it, and uses the link, which works once. It signs the account out everywhere: every session of the account is revoked, and the user then signs in with the new password. The account's other reset links stop working too. A token that does not exist, of another kind of link, or of an account that can no longer use it, is answered with 400 token_invalid, a link that has been used with 400 token_used, and one that has expired with 400 token_expired. The new password must have at least 12 characters, counted as Unicode code points once it is in NFKC, and must not be one of the 10,000 most common passwords, or the answer is 422 weak_password, which leaves the link as it was. Signing in, registering, changing a password, completing first-run setup, asking for a link that resets a password or verifies an email address, using one, and an instance admin's taking one as text share a rate limit of 20 requests a minute for each IP address. Registering and asking for a link that resets a password also have one of 10 a minute for each email address, and changing a password, asking for a link that verifies the signed-in account's email address, and an instance admin's taking a link as text one of 10 a minute for each account. The RateLimit headers say how much of the limit of the IP address, or of the account, is left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.reason is rate, whose RateLimit headers report the limit that it is over, that of the email address included, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

post.summary: Reset a password with a link

post.description: Creates an account with an email address, a display name, and a password, if the instance's signup policy lets anyone register: the policy that STORYCREEP_SIGNUP sets, or else the one that first-run setup chose. Until setup has completed, the answer is 403 setup_required, whatever the policy. Under closed the answer is 403 signup_closed, and under invite 403 invite_required, because only an invitation creates an account then; each comes whatever the request holds. An email address or a display name that its field does not allow is answered with 422 validation_failed. The password must have at least 12 characters, counted as Unicode code points once it is in NFKC, and must not be one of the 10,000 most common passwords, compared without regard to case, or the answer is 422 weak_password. Otherwise the answer is 202 without a body, whether or not the address has an account already, which then stays as it was, so that the answer does not tell whether an address has an account. On an instance that sends email, as GET /api/v1/instance says, a new account is emailed a link that verifies its address, which POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email uses, and an address that has an account already is emailed nothing. Signing in, registering, changing a password, completing first-run setup, asking for a link that resets a password or verifies an email address, using one, and an instance admin's taking one as text share a rate limit of 20 requests a minute for each IP address. Registering and asking for a link that resets a password also have one of 10 a minute for each email address, and changing a password, asking for a link that verifies the signed-in account's email address, and an instance admin's taking a link as text one of 10 a minute for each account. The RateLimit headers say how much of the limit of the IP address, or of the account, is left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.reason is rate, whose RateLimit headers report the limit that it is over, that of the email address included, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

patch.description: Changes a workspace's name, slug, or default locale; a field that the body leaves out, or sets to null, stays as it is. Only an owner or an admin of the workspace may, and anyone else with a role in it is answered with 403 insufficient_role. A workspace that does not exist, or in which the signed-in user's role is none, as it is for a user who is not a member or is a guest, is answered with 404 not_found, so that the answer does not tell whether it exists. A name or a default locale that its field does not allow is answered with 422 validation_failed. It needs a signed-in user: the session cookie that POST /api/v1/auth/login sets, or the answer is 401 unauthenticated. It changes something, so it also needs the session's CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header, or the answer is 403 csrf_failed.

parameters.description: The session's CSRF token, csrf_token, which signing in and GET /api/v1/auth/session return; without it the answer is 403 csrf_failed
